edge.title: Add NorMuon-lite (β2 0.8) and ramped Contra-Muon to Muown; retune
edge.summary: On top of #23's Muown, the orthogonalized direction update passes through two ported stages before the 0.2·√max(m,n) scale: Contra-Muon subtracts c_t·M/‖M‖_op (M = pre-polar Nesterov momentum of grad_v; c_t = 0.325 decaying linearly to 0 at step 1925) and restores the Frobenius norm, damping the gradient's dominant singular directions early in training; then NorMuon-lite (β2 = 0.80) evens out per-row update RMS (per column for mlp.proj) with a Frobenius restore. Because Muown pins all rows of v to one scheduled norm, this roughly equalizes per-row angular steps. Schedules are retuned — Muown lr 0.00325→0.0045, momentum 0.95→0.946, LR horizon 3165→3045, v-norm ramp over 3005 steps with power 0.9, attn.proj/mlp.fc v-norm targets ×1.5 — and train_steps drops 3090→3000, claimed at 2995.

changes.label: Contra-Muon with linear ramp-off
changes.detail: contra_coeff_schedule(self._global_step) = (0.65/2)·(1 − min(1, t/1925)); while nonzero, update = O − c_t·scale_to_unit_operator_norm(update_pre_ns) (5 power iterations), rescaled back to ‖O‖_F.

changes.label: NorMuon-lite on the direction update
changes.detail: _normuon_renorm (longer-axis mean-square EMA, rsqrt clamp 1e-10, Frobenius restore) with nor_muon_beta2=0.80 and an fp32 second_moment buffer, applied after contra and before the 0.2·√max(m,n) scale.

changes.label: V-norm schedule retuned
changes.detail: V_NORM_SCHEDULE_STEPS 3165 → 3005 and power 1.2 → 0.9 (faster early growth); family multipliers attn.proj 1 → 1.5, mlp.fc 1.0 → 1.5 (mlp.proj 3.333 kept).

changes.label: LR horizon 3165 → 3045
changes.detail: Same lr_eta power-0.9 cooldown; the LR is ≈3.5% of peak at the claimed step.

changes.label: train_steps 3090 → 3000, claim 2995
changes.detail: Validation every 5 steps during the last 25 steps; 2995 is the first such checkpoint passing the significance test.

changes.label: Docstrings, seeding, dead constants
changes.detail: Credits docstring, direction_scale arg removed with 0.2 hard-coded (same value), unused BETA2 constant, num_trials 30 → 1 with SEED = 2 (the 20 logs use SEED 0–19).

mechanisms.name: Contra-Muon (ramped, on the Muown direction)
mechanisms.explain: After Polar Express maps the Nesterov momentum M of grad_v to O, contra_coeff_schedule gives c_t = 0.325·(1 − min(1, t/1925)); while c_t > 0 the update becomes O − c_t·M/‖M‖_op (‖M‖_op from 5 power iterations started at the all-ones vector), rescaled back to ‖O‖_F. With O ≈ UVᵀ and M = UΣVᵀ each unit singular value becomes 1 − c_t·σᵢ/σ_max, so the gradient's dominant directions get relatively smaller steps early on, and the step returns to plain Muown by step 1925.

mechanisms.name: NorMuon-lite inside Muown
mechanisms.explain: _normuon_renorm applies #9's rule to the contra-adjusted polar update of v: an fp32 EMA (β2 = 0.80, i.e. lerp weight 0.2) of mean squared entries along the longer axis, multiplication by rsqrt(EMA) (clamp 1e-10) and restoration of the Frobenius norm. Since every row of v carries the same scheduled norm, equalizing per-row update RMS roughly equalizes per-row angular step sizes (per column for the wide mlp.proj), with a much shorter memory than #9's β2 = 0.95.

caveats: The README only lists per-seed losses; all constants here come from the code (20 logs, one trial each, SEED 0–19). The docstring's 'lr(t) = min(lr0, c·(t_end − t)^p)' is the same function as the inherited lr_eta (p = 0.9, knee at 30% of 3045). The lineage lists #10 as an influence, but the code (and README) port #9's PR #274 NorMuon-lite (mathematically identical to #10's normalizer, here with β2 0.80).
